chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'dawi quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Uthman and Ibn Abi Hamzah, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).
He said: I asked him, 'What is the first gift that is given to a believer?' He replied, 'The forgiveness of those who follow his corpse in his funeral procession.'

key_terms.يُتَحَفُّ: is gifted / is presented with a gift

ai.seo_question: What is the first gift a believer receives for their good character according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the attendance at one's funeral procession as the initial spiritual gift bestowed upon a believer, linking social piety directly to posthumous reward. This narration underscores the communal nature of salvation in Shia tradition, where the collective act of accompanying the deceased serves as a means of intercession and divine mercy for the deceased's followers.
